repose

/rih-POHZ/ - rhymes with suppose · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Repose means to rest or lie down.

After the harvest feast, the whole household reposed on mats in the shade, and even the dogs stopped patrolling.

Worked Example

In the museum's most famous portrait, the duchess reposes on a green divan, one book fallen shut in her hand and her eyes half-closed against the afternoon light. The painter, court records say, required her to hold that perfect stillness for three hours at a sitting.

Repose is the painter's word where lie down is the plain one: it carries a dignified, complete stillness — rest with composure in it. She is not napping or lounging; she reposes, and the elevated, literary register is exactly what a state portrait calls for.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rest: Rest is the plain, everyday word for stopping activity to recover — after practice, between shifts, on a park bench. Repose adds dignity and complete stillness to the same idea, which is why poems and portrait captions reach for it. A coffee break is rest; repose is rest held with composure.

recline: To recline is specifically to lean the body back — an airline seat, a dentist's chair, an elbow sunk in cushions. It names a posture and nothing more. Repose names a state: complete, composed stillness, holdable in any position, carrying a quiet dignity that recline never claims.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

toil: to labor long and hard

bustle: to move about with busy energy

Where it sits · how deep the stillness goes — lounge → repose → slumber

lounge vs. repose: To lounge is to idle in a loose, slouchy sprawl; repose goes further into stillness — complete, composed rest.

slumber vs. repose: Slumber goes past repose: the duchess reposing on the divan is awake and still, while a slumbering guest has crossed into sleep.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back, again

Root — pose

Root — pose: to rest, to pause (Late Latin pausare)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (back) + pose (to rest) = to settle back into rest. Late Latin repausare meant 'to rest again, to lay to rest'; the pose here is the resting kind, from pausare — so to repose is literally to put yourself back at rest.

Use the root in a new word: pause

Use the root in a new word: pause: She hit pause on the movie and let the kettle's whistle wind down before pouring.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Repose is rest in evening dress: choose it for portraits, poetry, and prose that wants dignity, and let rest or lie down do the daily work. Its cluster-mate respite names the break itself — a stretch of relief from strain — while repose names what you do during one.
